title: Sign-in tokens consume exactly once, expire on a bounded clock, and are superseded on remint
asA: operator whose emailed link might be intercepted, archived, or replayed
iWant: each link to work exactly one time within a short window and to become useless the moment I ask for a fresh link
soThat: a stolen or forwarded URL stops mattering as soon as I have moved past it

acceptanceCriteria.description: A token consumed by GET /login/verify cannot be consumed a second time; a repeat call with the same token returns 401 without issuing a session.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a token has been consumed once, issuing a session
acceptanceCriteria.when: GET /login/verify is called again with the same token value
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 401 and no Set-Cookie header is emitted

acceptanceCriteria.description: A token past its expiry cannot be consumed; GET /login/verify after the expiry window returns 401 without issuing a session.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a valid unconsumed token whose expiresAt is now in the past
acceptanceCriteria.when: GET /login/verify is called with that token
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 401 and no Set-Cookie header is emitted

acceptanceCriteria.description: The default token expiry window is fifteen minutes; the window is a project-configurable option on the magic-link manager and its effective value is enumerable at runtime.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a token is minted without a project override
acceptanceCriteria.then: the recorded expiresAt is fifteen minutes after the mint clock; when a project supplies expiryMs the recorded expiry matches the override

acceptanceCriteria.description: Minting a fresh token for a principal invalidates every prior unconsumed token for that principal; the previous URL cannot be exchanged after remint.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a principal has an unconsumed token T1 and requests a fresh sign-in link, minting T2
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 401 and no Set-Cookie header is emitted
